solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Away from her usual environment, Delia cooked all over France

indicators.note: all over means the scrambled name spreads around the next piece, wrapping it
cooked means the name Delia is prepared into a fresh arrangement of its letters

parts.note: F is the international abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: Delia Smith, the TV cook, on a culinary tour of France, far from her own kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns DELIA into AIELD, and 'all over' wraps that around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far from home or in unfamiliar territory is a standard sense of the adverb, as in 'travelled far afield'.

clue.text: Nothing offloaded from a boat on Thames heading upriver to ultimate destination

indicators.note: offloaded from means that zero is taken off the little boat phrase

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of Thames

parts.note: Rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river; up, in this down clue, turns it to read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Cargo unloaded from a Thames barge heading upstream to its final stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' does two jobs: river is RIO, and 'up' turns it to OIR in this down clue; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where livestock end up, their final stop, so it is wryly their ultimate destination.

clue.text: Orphaned artist in Bury

indicators.note: orphaned means losing a parent, here pa, a father

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A parentless artist who lives in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Lancashire, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, which is what burial means.

clue.text: Capricious, if cruel match

indicators.note: capricious means unpredictable and changeable, so the letters of if cruel are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unpredictable, cruel sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture but is the thing you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucifer is an old word for a friction match, named for the light-bringer.

clue.text: Bouquet is a parting purchase

indicators.note: parting means the little word a splits the following word in two by sitting in its middle

parts.note: purchase is a grip or leverage, and prise is to lever something open

explanation.surface: A farewell gift of flowers bought for someone leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a parting purchase' reads as a leaving present, but it says A parts PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is a compliment or commendation, so it is a synonym for acclaim or approval given.

clue.text: Blazing row over spilled fuel

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the scolding word above the rest

parts.note: to rag someone is to scold or row them; also a rage, as in losing one's rag

indicators.note: spilled means the letters of fuel are scattered

explanation.surface: An argument over spilled petrol that ends in a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' makes EFUL from fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Blazing can mean furiously angry, and rageful means full of fury.

clue.text: He knows nothing of smog (untreated) and air pollution

indicators.note: pollution means contamination or corruption, so the letters of the words beside it are messed up

parts.note: taken as written
the clue's own prefix un- (not) is lifted from untreated and mixed in
taken as written

explanation.surface: An environmental ignoramus who knows nothing about smog and air pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: The UN of 'untreated' joins SMOG and AIR in the mix; the blogger took 'treated' as the anagram signal and thought this a step too far.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, someone who lacks knowledge.

clue.text: Send out old weather report

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: report signals a word as heard spoken

parts.note: hail is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: Instructions to issue an outdated weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' makes HAIL heard as HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out is to send air out of the lungs.

clue.text: Jumble? It's cheap rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish, as a verb, means to trash, so the letters of it's cheap are knocked about

explanation.surface: Someone at a jumble sale dismissing the goods as cheap tat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'Jumble' as a loose definition: a pastiche is a medley of borrowed styles.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche can be a hotchpotch or medley of bits drawn from various sources, much like a jumble.

clue.text: Is a quarter of Leinster green before the surrounding country?

indicators.note: before places the green word ahead of the rest

parts.note: emerald is a bright green

indicators.note: a quarter of an eight-letter name is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Is Leinster, one of Ireland's four provinces, a green quarter of the country around it?
explanation.walkthrough: Leinster is one of Ireland's four provinces, so a quarter in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is nicknamed after its green landscape, and it is the nation that surrounds Leinster.

clue.text: Renowned vegetarian tucked into black pudding and hickory ham

indicators.note: tucked into says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, crossing word boundaries

explanation.surface: A famous vegetarian eating blood sausage and smoked ham, an absurd picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The name spans puddinG AND HIckory. Black pudding is a British blood sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi was a lifelong, committed vegetarian who wrote about the moral basis of meatless eating.

clue.text: Porridge mix

definitions.meaning: porridge is British slang for a prison term
to mix something is to agitate it with a spoon

explanation.surface: Instructions for making oat breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is British slang for time in prison (also a TV sitcom title); stir is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison slang supplies one sense, and the everyday verb for mixing with a spoon supplies the other.

clue.text: Score draw reported after easy-going encounter

indicators.note: after puts the spoken score behind the relaxed word

parts.note: easy-going and relaxed means free, as in a free and easy manner

indicators.note: reported says the football result is heard, not read

parts.note: a score draw where each side gets four goals is four-all

explanation.surface: A football match described: a goalscoring draw following a relaxed game.
explanation.walkthrough: A score draw is a drawn match with goals, here four-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly fight or contest open to everyone, so a kind of encounter or clash.

clue.text: Old Spice — out beyond doubt — produce once sold by Henry Cooper

definitions.text: produce once sold by Henry Cooper

parts.note: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice, a former (old) member of the Spice Girls

indicators.note: out tells us a letter goes out of the word for certain, dropping its final letter

parts.note: in cricket a batsman plumb lbw is out beyond any doubt; plumb means utterly

explanation.surface: A vintage aftershave brand, and the boxer Henry Cooper, who fronted adverts for Brut.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger reads PLUMB said aloud, with the homophone signal lost in editing; here 'out' drops its B. Henry Cooper, British boxer, had a greengrocer's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria plum is a popular British variety of the fruit, exactly the kind of produce a greengrocer sells.

clue.text: Bath fashioned with inlaid marquetry, plated in Middle East

indicators.note: with inlaid means the decorative word is set inside the rearranged spa name
fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters of Bath are rearranged

parts.note: boule (or boulle) is ornate inlay work of brass and tortoiseshell

explanation.surface: A bath decorated with inlay and plating, a luxury fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plated' means served on a plate, so the definition is a dish; boule is also spelt boulle, after the French cabinetmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabbouleh is a Levantine salad of bulgur, parsley and mint, a dish served up across the region.

clue.text: A dreadful pity about the French revolutionary being deviant

indicators.note: dreadful means awful, so the letters of pity are mangled

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the French word reads backwards

parts.note: la is the French for the

explanation.surface: A terrible pity about a deviant French revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' makes TYPI from pity, and 'revolutionary' turns LA into AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, departing from the norm, which is what deviant means.

clue.text: Workplace bribes including £500 in ones and even fifties

indicators.note: including means the bribes word holds the money-and-ones piece within it

parts.note: bungs are slang for bribes or backhanders

indicators.note: in places the money sum between the two ones

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals, so ones are two I's
L is the pound sign (libra) and D is 500 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: even says to take the second, fourth and sixth letters of fifties

explanation.surface: Corruption at work: cash bribes paid in single notes and fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: The £ sign is L from Latin libra, and D is Roman 500; the inner group sits inside the bribes word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A construction site is a place where builders work, so it is a kind of workplace.

clue.text: Animal purring by a fenced-in watering hole

indicators.note: fenced-in means the purring piece is enclosed by the pub

parts.note: a watering hole is slang for a pub or inn
purring is a low hum

explanation.surface: An animal purring beside a fenced waterhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' looks like a noun but is the adjective, meaning brutish.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means brutish and unfeeling, the same as cruel and beastly behaviour.

clue.text: Solution doesn't strike a chord

parts.note: doesn't, meaning does not, gives no
to strum is to sweep across guitar strings, striking a chord

explanation.surface: An answer that fails to resonate with anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike a chord' is meant figuratively but read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy or pet scheme, a supposed cure-all for a problem.

clue.text: Somewhat jazzy, deconstructionist music

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of avant-garde music: rather jazzy and deconstructionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is Louisiana Creole dance music featuring accordion and washboard, a genre of music.

clue.text: In theory doctor's posh, yet embodying extremes of hoi polloi

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters that follow are rearranged
extremes of means the first and last letters of hoi polloi

parts.note: the apostrophe s on the signal word is read as a letter for the mix

explanation.surface: A snobbish doctor who nonetheless treats the common people, in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter borrows the 's of 'doctor's', the anagram signal itself, as an S for the mix with POSH, YET and HI (outer letters of 'hoi polloi'); 'embodying' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation awaiting proof, essentially a theory or supposition.

clue.text: Pinch top off mop

indicators.note: top off means the first letter of the stealing word is removed

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, and swipe is slang for stealing

explanation.surface: Instructions for cleaning: remove the head from a mop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' looks like part of a cleaning instruction, but it drops the S from SWIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop a surface is to wipe it clean, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sound of revolution in West greeting holy man

parts.note: hi is a greeting
RR stands for Right Reverend, a title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A holy man greeted in the western part of a country during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising but means turning, as of a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is the buzzing noise of something spinning rapidly, like a fan or propeller.

clue.text: Starter of blue cheese left in confusion

indicators.note: starter of means only the first letter of the word blue is taken
in tells us the abbreviation for left goes inside the cheese

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A cheeseboard mix-up: a blue cheese left among the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks culinary but means the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum, means uproar and chaos, a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Early asparagus tips recipe misled listener

indicators.note: tips here are the leading letters of early and asparagus, like the tips of spears
misled means the letters of recipe are sent astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook led astray by a recipe for early asparagus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misled' makes RPIECE from recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An earpiece is the part of a phone or headset that you hear through, a device for listening.

clue.text: Available digitally

definitions.meaning: something ready and at your disposal is available
digitally read literally means by the fingers, so placed on the hand

explanation.surface: A modern product that can be got online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digitally' means by the digits, the fingers, not by computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ready and accessible, and read literally it means resting on the fingers' hand.

clue.text: With no concern for right or wrong, Marple's all but last following up scent

definitions.text: With no concern for right or wrong

indicators.note: following puts the detective's letter after the turned smell
up says the smell word is read backwards

parts.note: a scent or pleasant smell is an aroma

indicators.note: all but last here means the letter just before the end of the name Marple: its penultimate

explanation.surface: Miss Marple, Agatha Christie's sleuth, ruthlessly following up a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but last' means penultimate, giving L from MARPLE; 'up' turns AROMA into AMORA, though this is an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone lacking any sense of ethics, unconcerned with moral distinctions.
